questions.q: What is the defining difference between a managed package and an unlocked package?
options: A managed package's Apex code is obfuscated/hidden from the installing org and uses a namespace to prevent naming collisions, unlike an unlocked package
Managed packages cannot be versioned at all
Unlocked packages can only be installed once per org
There is no real difference between the two package types
questions.explain: Managed packages hide their Apex implementation from the installing org and rely on a namespace to prevent collisions with the customer's own components — the opposite of an unlocked package's visible, developer-controlled metadata.

questions.q: What limitation applies to a managed package version while it's still in beta?
options: It cannot be installed anywhere, even for testing
It can be installed for testing but can't be listed for general AppExchange distribution or installed by customers through the normal channel
It automatically expires after 7 days like a scratch org
It can only be installed into a Dev Hub, never a regular org
questions.explain: A beta version is installable for testing purposes, but it's not eligible for general AppExchange listing or normal customer installation until it's promoted to released.

questions.q: What user permission must you hold in the Dev Hub to promote a package version to released?
options: System Administrator, with no additional permission needed
"Modify All Data"
No permission is required for promotion
"Promote a Package Version to Released"
questions.explain: Promoting a package version to released specifically requires the "Promote a Package Version to Released" user permission in the Dev Hub associated with the package.

questions.q: What happens if you try to promote the same package version number to released a second time, or try to revert a released version back to beta?
options: It's allowed, since promotion can always be undone
Salesforce Support can always manually revert it on request
It's not possible — you can promote and release a given version number exactly once, and the action can't be undone
The version automatically reverts after 90 days
questions.explain: Promotion to released is a one-way action: a given package version number can be promoted and released exactly once, and there is no way to undo it or revert it back to beta.

questions.q: What replaced the older first-generation managed packaging workflow that required a dedicated packaging org?
options: Second-generation managed packaging, created and versioned directly from a Dev Hub-connected source-driven project
Unlocked packages, which eliminated managed packages entirely
Change sets
The Metadata Coverage Report
questions.explain: Second-generation managed packaging replaced the first-generation workflow's dependency on a separate packaging org, instead creating and versioning managed packages directly from a Dev Hub-connected project via the CLI.
